title: [Product Bug] Show validation error for invalid email format fails on WebKit
rootCause: In WebKit, the email input element's built-in browser validation (`type="email"`) can prevent the form 'submit' event from firing if the value does not match a valid email format, or WebKit handles native validation differently, preventing custom client-side validation logic from running on submit.
suggestedFix: Add the 'novalidate' attribute to the form element or handle the input type so native browser validation doesn't block the submit event in WebKit.
testToValidate: Show validation error for invalid email format fails on WebKit
reasoning: 1. Look at src/client/app.ts where the form is rendered: `<form id="registration-form" novalidate>`. Wait, novalidate is present on the form, but let's check how WebKit interacts with email input types and submit events. Alternatively, WebKit might treat type="email" strictly during form submission or value checking. Looking closely at `field` function in src/client/app.ts: `<input name="name" type="type" ...>` vs `<input name="email" type="email" required />`. Wait, `field` function signature is `function field(name: string, label: string, type = 'text', required = false): string`. When calling `field('email', 'Email address', 'email', true)`, it outputs `type="email" required`. In WebKit, an input with `type="email"` enforces native validation constraints when submitting unless overridden or handled, or the form's novalidate attribute prevents it. Wait, the form has `novalidate`. Let's examine why WebKit fails: Safari/WebKit's built-in handling of input type email combined with how `.value` is checked or how form submission is intercepted might differ. Wait, looking at `showFormErrors`: `if (!email.value.includes('@'))`. In WebKit, typing an invalid email into an input of `type="email"` can sometimes cause `.value` to be empty string `""` or trigger native constraints before the JS event listener executes depending on interaction. Changing the email input type to `type="text"` or ensuring native validation interference is avoided resolves WebKit discrepancies since custom validation via `.includes('@')` is used instead of native browser email validation.
